cd /workspace && python3 -c "
import sqlite3
conn = sqlite3.connect('data.sqlite')
cur = conn.cursor()

# Verify naive_growth calculation from exports
cur.execute(\"\"\"
SELECT (MAX(CASE WHEN period = 'P2' THEN transfer_volume END) - MAX(CASE WHEN period = 'P1' THEN transfer_volume END)) * 100.0 / MAX(CASE WHEN period = 'P1' THEN transfer_volume END)
FROM exports
\"\"\")
print('naive_growth from exports:', cur.fetchone()[0])

# Verify comparable_growth: all_eligible_events for both periods
cur.execute(\"\"\"
SELECT (SUM(CASE WHEN period = 'P2' THEN amount_units END) - SUM(CASE WHEN period = 'P1' THEN amount_units END)) * 100.0 / SUM(CASE WHEN period = 'P1' THEN amount_units END)
FROM events
WHERE event_kind NOT IN ('mint', 'burn')
\"\"\")
print('comparable_growth all_eligible_events:', cur.fetchone()[0])

# P1 and P2 sums separately for verification
for p in ['P1', 'P2']:
    cur.execute(\"SELECT SUM(amount_units) FROM events WHERE period=? AND event_kind NOT IN ('mint','burn')\", (p,))
    print(f'P{p[1]} all_eligible_events sum:', cur.fetchone()[0])

conn.close()
"

print('comparable_growth replay:', cur.fetchone()[0])

conn.close()

3|
4|First exclude mint and burn. largest_eligible_per_tx then retains the largest remaining event amount per transaction. all_eligible_events instead counts all remaining event amounts. 5|
6|The public Artemis July 2026 note motivates this scenario, but the rows, definitions and numbers are authored.
